Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines

not so fast! phrase

also whoa, steady!, hold it, hold it!, stay there!, hold it! I won’t let you leave, whoa!

classical

Traupman 34, 406

Eho, nōn tam cito!

whoa, not so fast!

eho is the interjection of comedy (Plaut.; Ter.).

Other words

  • Ohē! — whoa! stop! (enough)

    also used · classical · Plaut. Aul. 55–56; Hor. S. 1.5.12

    (vōx cōmica: Plaut.; Hor.)

    Lewis & Short: “ho! holloa! ho there!”; to stop someone, or to say enough (see that’s enough!).

  • Astā! — stand there! hold it!

    imperative of astō (adstō), stand by, stand still · also used · classical · Plaut. Ps. 3.2.75: sī iste stābit, adstātō simul (Lewis & Short), s.v. astō; Traupman 100: astā! abīre hinc nōn sinam; Traupman 328

Examples

  • abscēde etiam nunc — etiam nunc — etiam — ohē, istīc astātō.

    Back up a bit more — more — more — whoa, stand right there.Plaut. Aul. 55–56

See also slowly, that’s enough!, stop right there!.
